Definition: to rebel; hence (through the idea of maltreating) to whip, i.e. lash (self with wings, as the ostrich in running)
BiblicalUsage: mârâʼ is to rebel, and by a second picture to lash oneself, as the ostrich does with her wings in running. In Zephaniah 3:1 woe is pronounced on the filthy and polluted oppressing city, and in Job 39:18 the ostrich lifts herself up on high and scorns the horse and his rider. The word joins rebellion to a creature showing off its speed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârâʼ warns me that rebellion can look like strength, like an ostrich lifting herself high, and I hold that the city that will not be cleansed will be judged.
